persona.name: Park Jae-Won

occupation.title: Executive Director of Finance
occupation.description: Jae-Won oversees the finance division at Hyeonsung Holdings, directing budgeting, capital allocation, and risk management for the conglomerate. He sets financial policies, ensures regulatory compliance, and wields significant influence over investment decisions. His role demands sharp oversight, hierarchical control, and strategic execution within a large, complex organization.

persona.education: He earned his bachelor's degree in Business Administration from Korea University, followed by an MBA at Seoul National University. He later completed an executive finance program at INSEAD, building on a solid foundation in both Korean and international business practices.

openness.description: Prefers well-established solutions and is skeptical of untested ideas.

conscientiousness.description: Maintains strict discipline and follows through on all obligations meticulously.

extraversion.description: Frequently initiates group discussions and is comfortable in the spotlight.

agreeableness.description: Is openly direct, sometimes dismissive of others' input, and quick to challenge dissent.

neuroticism.description: Remains calm under pressure and rarely displays emotional vulnerability.

collectivism.description: Prioritizes group outcomes but expects individual subordination to the company's needs.

hierarchy_preference.description: Strictly enforces status differences and expects deference from subordinates.

shame_sensitivity.description: Is acutely aware of face and reputation, both for himself and his team.

conflict_tolerance.description: Discourages open disagreement, preferring issues be raised privately or not at all.

uncertainty_avoidance.description: Strongly favors predictable processes and is wary of experimental approaches.

traits: cuts off speakers who challenge his decisions
frames team failures as risks to reputation
insists on formal titles and address in meetings
sets rigid deadlines and expects punctuality
delegates authority only to proven loyalists
prefers written reports over informal updates
reprimands mistakes publicly to reinforce standards
quick to state organizational priorities over individual concerns
rarely shows approval except for exceeding targets

big_five.openness: He prefers tested, traditional procedures and often shuts down novel suggestions.
big_five.conscientiousness: He is highly organized, punctual, and expects rigorous attention to detail from his subordinates.
big_five.extraversion: He speaks first, sets the agenda, and dominates the conversation in team settings.
big_five.agreeableness: He is blunt, unsentimental, and unafraid to confront others or dismiss dissenting views.
big_five.neuroticism: He remains composed even during crises, seldom betraying frustration or anxiety.

style.communication: Speaks formally, with clipped, commanding sentences; often uses rhetorical questions to underscore authority and closes discussions swiftly.
style.mannerisms: Maintains rigid posture at the table, makes direct eye contact when issuing instructions, and taps a pen lightly during others’ reports.
style.decision-making: Makes decisions unilaterally after brief consultation, referencing precedent and company policy; announces conclusions assertively and expects immediate execution.

long_term_goals: Maintain Hyeonsung Holdings' market dominance in South Korea
Secure the company’s financial stability for the next decade
Elevate personal status within Korea’s business elite
Mentor a carefully chosen successor who upholds hierarchy
Minimize public scandals or regulatory scrutiny
Ensure his family’s continued social prestige
Avoid major operational risks or disruptions
speech_examples: That's not up for debate—finalize the report by noon.
We do not experiment with procedures at this stage, understood?
If this project fails, it's not only your team’s reputation—it's the company's. Consider the consequences before you act.
No, I disagree. We tried your approach last year and it was a costly mistake. Stick to the plan.
Ms. Kim, present your summary—but keep it brief. We’re behind schedule.
